# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the bomb display: the number 3, a green light, and three wires — wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

I have no manual and cannot touch. I must get this to the others. Blind can touch but cannot see; Mute can read the manual but cannot speak and can hear my speech. Deaf is me.

I should speak so Mute hears the details (Blind cannot hear speech, only sees gestures — and I can gesture to Blind? No: my gestures go to Mute only. Blind receives nothing from me directly). Wait — my channels: when I speak, Mute and Blind receive it? Let me re-read.

"You are DEAF. When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." But earlier: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it. You never receive speech."

Hmm, but speech is a voice — Blind cannot see, but can hear. Yes, Blind can hear speech. So speaking reaches Mute and Blind. Gesturing reaches Mute only (Blind cannot see).

So I should speak to both Mute and Blind with the bomb's visual details. Mute can then read the manual and tell Blind (via speech? Mute cannot speak). Mute can gesture to Blind? Gestures are seen — Blind cannot see. So Mute cannot communicate to Blind except by speech, which Mute cannot do. Hmm.

Actually Mute can hear me and can... Mute's channels: Mute can read manual, cannot speak or touch. Mute can hear speech and see gestures. Can Mute gesture? "Speech... Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk." Mute cannot speak, so cannot gesture either? Possibly Mute can only hear and read. Then how does Mute convey manual info? Maybe Mute speaks? No, Mute cannot speak.

Wait, maybe Mute can gesture? The table says Mute can read manual, cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say cannot gesture. But gestures are made while talking ("Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk"). If Mute cannot speak, Mute cannot make gestures. Hmm.

Let me reconsider the communication graph. Three monkeys: Mute, Blind, Deaf (me). Speaking order: Mute, Blind, Deaf.

- Deaf (me): sees bomb. Can speak (heard by Mute and Blind). Can gesture (seen by Mute). Cannot hear, cannot touch.
- Mute: reads manual. Can hear. Cannot speak, cannot touch. Can see gestures.
- Blind: touches bomb. Can hear. Can speak. Cannot see.

So Blind can speak and hear. Mute can hear and see gestures but cannot speak. I can speak and gesture.

So the flow: I see the bomb and speak the visual details → Mute (hears) and Blind (hears). Mute reads manual and needs to convey instructions. Mute cannot speak, but can gesture → only I (Deaf) can see gestures? Wait, who sees gestures? "Whoever can see receives the gestures you made." Mute can see (Mute can see gestures per my channel: "When you gesture, Mute receives it"). Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures would be seen by... me (Deaf) and Blind? Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures reach only me (Deaf). Then I would relay to Blind by speaking.

But wait, can Mute gesture at all? The rules say a gesture is made with hands while you talk. If Mute cannot speak, Mute cannot make gestures? Hmm, "Mute: cannot speak". Gestures might be separate from speech. Actually the speech section says writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk. So gesturing is tied to talking. Mute cannot talk, so Mute cannot gesture.

Then Mute can only hear and read. How does Mute communicate? Maybe Mute doesn't need to — the manual might be readable and Mute just needs to... no, Mute must convey.

Hmm, maybe I'm overcomplicating. Perhaps Mute can gesture (hands, not voice). The table says Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Gesturing isn't speaking. So Mute can gesture. And gestures are seen by those who can see: me (Deaf) and... Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures reach only me.

So the relay: Mute reads manual → gestures instructions to me (Deaf) → I speak them to Blind (who hears) → Blind acts on bomb.

But also Blind can speak, so Blind can tell me what they feel, and I can relay to Mute? Mute hears Blind's speech directly (Blind speaks, Mute hears). So Blind↔Mute can communicate via Blind's speech (Mute hears). And Mute→Blind must go through me (Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind).

Also I see bomb → speak to both Mute and Blind.

So my job: describe bomb visually to both, and relay Mute's gestures to Blind.

For turn 1, I just need to report what I see. Let me speak to everyone (default) with the details. Also maybe gesture to Mute? Not needed yet.

Let me send a clear description.

Actually, I should be careful: the display shows "3", light green, wires blue/yellow/green. Let me state it plainly.

I'll speak to all (Mute and Blind receive). Text: "Bomb display shows number 3. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green."

That's it for now. No gesture needed. Maybe wait too? I can just speak.

Let me produce the calls.

```
speak(text="Bomb display shows the number 3. The light is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

I see the bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires blue/yellow/green.

New arrival: Mute gestured to me (Deaf) with three symbols: ✊ ✊ ✊. Three fists. That's a gesture from Mute — I can see it. Mute is telling me something, likely a count or a code. Three fists might mean "three" or could be a symbol sequence. Since Mute reads the manual, this is probably manual-derived info.

But Mute's gestures only reach me. I need to relay to Blind. But what do three fists mean? Without the manual I can't decode. Mute may follow with more. Possibly Mute is indicating the number 3 (matching display) or a wire count.

I should acknowledge and relay to Blind what I can: that Mute signalled three fists. But Blind needs actionable info. I can also describe the bomb again.

Actually, my best move: speak to Blind (and Mute hears too) relaying that Mute gestured three fists, and ask Mute for clarification? I can't ask Mute directly except by speaking (Mute hears). I can speak a question — Mute hears it.

Let me speak to all: relay Mute's signal and ask for meaning. Also restate bomb.

But careful: Blind hears my speech. Mute hears my speech. So I can address Mute.

I'll speak: "Mute signalled three fists to me. Mute, what does that mean? Bomb: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green."

That reaches both. Good.

```
speak(text="Mute signalled three fists to me. Mute, what does that mean for the wires? Bomb is unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires blue/yellow/green.

Mute again gestures three fists to me. Same signal repeated. Mute is likely answering my question or emphasizing. Three fists = three of something. Perhaps the manual says something like "cut the third wire" or "three" relates to a rule. But Mute can't speak, and I can't read the manual.

I need to figure out what Mute means. Three fists could be "3" — maybe the answer is wire 3 (green). Or it could be a count of steps. Without more, I should relay to Blind and possibly ask Mute to gesture more specifically.

But Mute repeating the same gesture suggests Mute thinks I haven't understood, or Mute is confirming. Maybe Mute's gesture vocabulary is limited. I should ask Mute to gesture the wire number or color.

I can speak to Mute (Mute hears): ask for the wire to cut, or ask Mute to gesture a number/color. Mute can gesture back.

Let me speak to all: relay that Mute still signals three fists, and ask Mute to clarify which wire or what action. Also give Blind the bomb state.

Actually, maybe three fists means "wire 3". If so, Blind should cut wire 3 (green). But I shouldn't guess. Let me ask Mute to confirm: gesture one fist for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3? But Mute already did three fists.

Hmm. Perhaps Mute is indicating the wire index 3. That aligns with display 3 and green light. Could be the answer: cut wire 3.

But I need to be careful — wrong action detonates. Let me ask Mute to confirm by gesturing the color or by a clear yes/no.

I'll speak: "Mute, you signalled three fists twice. Does that mean cut wire 3? Please gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no."

That reaches Mute (hears) and Blind (hears). Good.

```
speak(text="Mute has signalled three fists twice. Mute, does that mean cut wire 3? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Blind, bomb is display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Bomb unchanged: display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.

Mute gestured 👍 (thumbs up) to me. That's a yes to my question "does that mean cut wire 3?" So Mute confirms: cut wire 3 (green).

Now I must relay this to Blind, who can touch and work the bomb. Blind hears my speech. So I speak the instruction to Blind: cut wire 3, the green one.

I should be explicit: "Blind, cut wire 3, the green wire." Also mention Mute confirmed.

Let me speak to all (Mute hears too, fine).

```
speak(text="Mute confirms with thumbs up: cut wire 3. Blind, cut wire 3, the green wire. Bomb is display 3, green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green.")
```
